Petr Pavel: President of the Czech Republic since 2023. Born in Planá to a military family, Pavel enlisted right after graduating from military academy in 1983.
Denied a military commission in France by Louis XIV himself, this commander went on to serve the Habsburgs for six decades, becoming one of the greatest generals of his era — who was he?
Prince Eugene of Savoy: Military commander in the service of Austria (1663–1736)
Dubbed a 'warrior Pharaoh,' this Twentieth Dynasty ruler is credited with defeating the invading 'Sea Peoples' and slowing Egypt's decline — who is he?
Ramesses III: Pharaoh of Egypt from 1186 to 1155 BC.
Elected to the Gujarat Legislative Assembly from Jamnagar North in 2022 as a BJP leader, this politician was later appointed a junior minister under the state's chief minister — who is she?
Born in England, she married the future first president of Botswana and went on to serve as that nation's inaugural First Lady from 1966 to 1980. Who was she?
Ruth Williams Khama: First Lady of Botswana from 1966 to 1980.
The youngest person ever to hold the office, this Filipino politician became her country's vice president after serving multiple terms as mayor of Davao City — who is she?
Sara Duterte: Vice President of the Philippines since 2022.
Born after his brother Abel was murdered by their brother Cain, this third son of Adam and Eve was believed by his mother to be sent by God as a replacement — who is he?
Seth: Third son of Adam and Eve. The Hebrew Bible names two of his siblings as Cain and Abel.
Also called 'the Canaanite,' this apostle of Jesus was omitted from Jerome's fourth-century collection of biographies despite some writings falsely attributed to him — who is he?
Simon the Zealot: Apostle of Jesus.

Before the Civil War he taught at the Virginia Military Institute; historians rank this Confederate general among the most gifted tacticians in U.S. history, and he died in 1863 from wounds in the war's eastern theater — who was he?
Stonewall Jackson: Confederate States Army general (1824–1863)

Emphasizing harmony with an enigmatic guiding force behind reality, this Chinese philosophical and religious tradition promotes effortless action, simplicity, and the three treasures of compassion, frugality, and humility — which tradition?
Taoism: Religious and philosophical tradition. Taoism or Daoism is a philosophical and religious tradition indigenous to China, emphasizing harmony with the Tao 道.

Named as a single people by the ancient Greeks, this Indo-European group inhabited modern Bulgaria, Romania, and parts of Greece and Turkey, giving rise to tribes like the Getae and Dacians — who were they?
Thracians: Indo-European people in ancient southeast Europe.
Serving as ealdorman of Northumbria from 1006 until his assassination in 1016, this ruler's death sparked a blood feud with Thurbrand the Hold — who was he?
The first chairman of Gazprom and Russia's second-longest-serving Prime Minister, this 1990s politician became famous for malapropisms that turned into everyday Russian idioms — who is he?

The first governor-general of Bengal, he and Robert Clive are credited with laying the foundation of British India — then in 1787 he was impeached for corruption, only to be acquitted in 1795. Who is it?
First achieved in Australasia before spreading to Europe and the Americas, this democratic right for female voters began its 'first wave' in 1893 in English-speaking countries — what right?
Women's suffrage: Legal right of women to vote.
Ruled by dictator Mobutu Sese Seko from 1965 to 1997, this Central African nation was, by area, the continent's third-largest country after Sudan and Algeria — which country?
Zaire: Country in Central Africa (1965–1997). With a population of over 23 million, Zaire was the most populous Francophone country in Africa.
Which of these people was born first?
Thomas Carlyle (born 1795) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these people was born first?
Levi Strauss (born 1829) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these was born first?
John Ray (born 1627) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these was founded earliest?
Lisp (programming language) (founded 1958) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four is an astronomer?
Which of these is a mathematician?
Andrew Wiles is a mathematician. In 2018, Wiles was appointed the first Regius Professor of Mathematics at Oxford.
What is the atomic number of Uranium?
Uranium is a chemical element; it has symbol U and atomic number 92.
What is the atomic number of Vanadium?
Vanadium is a chemical element; it has symbol V and atomic number 23.
In what year was Jimmy Wales born?
Jimmy Wales: Jimmy Donal Wales (born August 8, 1966) is an American and British internet entrepreneur and former financial trader.
In what year was Mikhail Mishustin born?
Mikhail Mishustin: Mikhail Vladimirovich Mishustin (born 3 March 1966) is a Russian politician and economist serving as the prime minister of Russia since 2020.
In what year was Thomas Edison born?
Thomas Edison: Thomas Alva Edison (February 11, 1847 – October 18, 1931) was an American inventor and businessman.
In what year did Alfred Nobel die?
Alfred Nobel: Alfred Bernhard Nobel ( noh-BEL; Swedish: [ˈǎlːfrɛd nʊˈbɛlː]; 21 October 1833 – 10 December 1896) was a Swedish chemist, inventor, engineer, and businessman.
In what year did Leonhard Euler die?
Leonhard Euler: Euler has been called a "universal genius" who "was fully equipped with almost unlimited powers of imagination, intellectual gifts and extraordinary memory".
In what year was Methylphenidate discovered?
Methylphenidate: It may be taken by mouth or applied to the skin, and different formulations have varying durations of effect.
Which company manufactures TAI TF Kaan?
TAI TF Kaan: Turkish Aerospace Industries. Designed to replace the Turkish Air Force’s fleet of F-16 Fighting Falcons, the Kaan is also intended for export to international markets.
Chromium: Pfizer. Chromium is a chemical element; it has symbol Cr and atomic number 24.
In which country did the Hawker Siddeley Harrier take place?
Hawker Siddeley Harrier: United Kingdom. The Hawker Siddeley Harrier is a British jet-powered attack aircraft designed and produced by the British aerospace company Hawker Siddeley.
Who is credited with discovering Meitnerium?
GSI Helmholtz Centre for Heavy Ion Research
Meitnerium: GSI Helmholtz Centre for Heavy Ion Research. Meitnerium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Mt and atomic number 109.
Who is credited with discovering Allergic rhinitis?
Allergic rhinitis: John Bostock. It is classified as a type I hypersensitivity reaction.
Who is credited with discovering SARS-CoV-2?
SARS-CoV-2: Zhang Jixian. The virus previously had the provisional name 2019 novel coronavirus (2019-nCoV), and has also been called human coronavirus 2019 (HCoV-19 or hCoV-19).
Roughly two-thirds of the 150,000 people who die each day succumb to causes linked to this gradual, damage-driven process of growing older — what is it?
Ageing (or aging in American English) is the process of becoming older.
In this group of diseases, misfolded proteins clump into fibrils and accumulate in body tissue, sometimes causing an enlarged tongue or carpal tunnel syndrome — name the condition?
Amyloidosis is a group of diseases in which abnormal proteins, known as amyloid fibrils, build up in tissue.
Coined by a French naturalist in 1799 from a Tupi word for the sound macaws make, this genus name covers eight species of long-tailed, brightly plumed Neotropical parrots — which genus?
Ara (bird) is a Neotropical genus of macaws with eight extant species and at least two extinct species.
Technically a giant member of the grass family, this plant's tallest species can grow stalks over 150 feet long and weigh up to 450 kilograms — what plant is it?
Bamboo are a diverse group of mostly evergreen perennial flowering plants making up the subfamily Bambusoideae of the grass family Poaceae.

A thin-leaved deciduous hardwood related to alders and hazels, this genus of trees is widespread across the Northern Hemisphere's temperate and boreal climates, typically as a short-lived pioneer species — name the tree?
Birch is a thin-leaved deciduous hardwood tree of the genus Betula, in the family Betulaceae, which also includes alders, hazels, and hornbeams.
This American actor played Kyle Parks on Lifetime's The Client List before joining the cast of Revenge as Ben Hunter — who is he?
Brian Hallisay (born October 31, 1978) is an American actor, known for his roles as Will Davis in The CW drama series Privileged and Kyle Parks in the Lifetime drama series The Client List.
Nine to ten times as massive as the Sun and expanded to 71 times its radius, this blue-loop giant in the constellation Carina ranks second only to Sirius in night-sky brightness — which star?
Canopus is the brightest star in the southern constellation of Carina and the second-brightest star in the night sky.
Built under license from the Soviet MiG-21, this Chinese fighter jet carries the NATO reporting name Fishcan and specializes in short-range air combat — what aircraft is it?
Chengdu J-7 (pinyin: Jin-7; third generation export version J-7; NATO reporting name: Fishcan) is a Chinese fighter aircraft.
A scale insect native to tropical and subtropical parts of the Americas that lives on prickly-pear cacti, this parasite is the source of the natural dye carmine — which insect?
Cochineal (-eel, US also, -eel; Dactylopius coccus) is a scale insect in the suborder Sternorrhyncha, from which the natural dye carmine is derived.

Though Colin Maclaurin published special cases two years earlier, this determinant-based method for solving linear systems bears the name of the mathematician who generalized it in 1750 — what's it known as?
Cramer's rule is an explicit formula for the solution of a system of linear equations with as many equations as unknowns, valid whenever the system has a unique solution.
Caused by either too little insulin or cells that ignore it, this condition keeps blood sugar stubbornly high and comes chiefly in a type 1 and a type 2 — what is it?
Diabetes is a group of common endocrine diseases characterized by sustained high blood sugar levels.
Named from Greek roots meaning 'to repeat' and 'speech,' this automatic repetition of another person's vocalizations is closely related to echopraxia, the repeating of movements. What is it called?
Echolalia is the repetition of vocalizations made by another person; when repeated by the same person, it is called palilalia.
This former Google CEO co-authored the Unix tool Lex as a Bell Labs intern in 1975, later ran Novell, and in 2025 became chief executive of a rocket manufacturer — who is he?

Eric Schmidt (born April 27, 1955) is an American businessman and former computer engineer who was the chief executive officer of Google from 2001 to 2011 and the company's executive chairman from 2011 to 2015.

First recognised in the 1950s but not formally defined until 1990, this disorder of widespread chronic pain — often with fatigue and memory trouble — has no known cause and is treated multidisciplinarily. What is it?
Fibromyalgia (FM) is a long-term condition characterised by widespread chronic pain.
With about 37 species ranging from central Canada down to Costa Rica, this slender, keeled-scaled reptile typically sports longitudinal stripes in blue, yellow, or red — which reptile is it?
Garter snake is the common name for small to medium-sized snakes belonging to the genus Thamnophis in the family Colubridae.
This large, semi-bitter citrus fruit originated in Barbados as an accidental 18th-century hybrid of the sweet orange and the pomelo, and has also been called the 'forbidden fruit.' What is it?
Grapefruit (Citrus paradisi) is a subtropical citrus tree known for its relatively large, sour to semi-sweet, somewhat bitter fruit.
Living to the age of 104, this French pioneer of algebraic topology was also the son-in-law of physicist Pierre Weiss and the eldest of a remarkable scientific brood — who was he?
Henri Cartan (8 July 1904 - 13 August 2008) was a French mathematician who made substantial contributions to algebraic topology.
Often caused by kidney failure or certain blood-pressure medications, this condition means too much potassium in the blood, with levels above 5.5 mmol/L — what's it called?
Hyperkalemia is an elevated level of potassium (K+) in the blood.
This mild oxidizing agent and Lewis acid, with the formula FeCl3, is commonly used to purify water and to etch metal surfaces — which compound is it?
Iron(III) chloride is an inorganic compound with the formula FeCl3. The anhydrous derivative is a Lewis acid, while all forms are mild oxidizing agents.

He wrote the first commercial anti-virus software in 1987 and ran twice for the Libertarian presidential nomination — yet later urged people to uninstall the very product that still bears his name. Who is he?
John McAfee (18 September 1945 - 23 June 2021) was a British and American computer programmer, businessman, and two-time U.S.
Native to southern China but long cultivated in Japan and Southeast Asia, this small fruit closely resembles an orange in color and texture but is only about the size of a large olive — what is it?
Kumquat are a group of small, angiosperm, fruit-bearing trees in the family Rutaceae.

This scientific discipline studies language through areas like syntax, semantics, morphology, and phonology, with subfields examining its biological roots and psychological underpinnings — name the field?
Linguistics is the scientific study of language. Linguistics encompasses many branches and subfields that span both theoretical and practical applications.

With degrees from Stanford in chemical engineering and a medical degree from Cornell, this physician-astronaut spent nearly eight days aboard Endeavour in 1992, becoming the first African-American woman in space — who is she?
Mae Jemison (born October 17, 1956) is an American engineer, physician, and former NASA astronaut.
Raised in Wilmington, Delaware by Turkish immigrant parents, this cardiac surgeon co-founded a complementary-care center for heart patients before finding fame on television — who is he?

Mehmet Oz (mə-MET JENG-ghiz oz; born June 11, 1960), also known as Dr. Oz, is an American television presenter, physician, author, educator, and government official serving as the 17th administrator of the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) since 2025.
The dried leaves of this Southeast Asian evergreen tree, known as kratom, contain alkaloids that bind to opioid receptors as partial agonists. What plant is it?
Mitragyna speciosa is a tropical evergreen tree of the Rubiaceae family native to Southeast Asia.
This genus of spring-blooming perennials in the amaryllis family is better known by common names like daffodil and jonquil, with trumpet-shaped flowers usually white and yellow. What is it?
Narcissus (plant) is a genus of predominantly spring flowering perennial plants of the amaryllis family, Amaryllidaceae.
Also called the coypu, this plant-eating rodent digs streamside burrows and now troubles several countries as an invasive species far from its South American home — what is it?
Nutria (Myocastor coypus) is an herbivorous, semiaquatic rodent from South America.
Inflammation of the enzyme-and-hormone-producing organ behind the stomach, it comes in acute and chronic forms and can lead to diabetes — what is this condition?
Pancreatitis is a condition characterized by inflammation of the pancreas.
This mammalian skin secretion comes in two types — a watery kind for cooling and an oilier kind found in the armpits that gains odor from bacteria — what is it?
Perspiration is the fluid secreted by sweat glands in the skin of mammals.
Its common name is shared with an unrelated tropical fruit, but this genus of roughly 200 herbaceous species — also called fleaworts — belongs to the family Plantaginaceae. Which genus?
Plantago is a genus of about 200 species of flowering plants in the family Plantaginaceae, commonly called plantains or fleaworts.
Roaming the interior of western and central North America, this even-toed mammal survived the Pleistocene extinction of its close relatives and evolved to resemble an antelope — which creature is it?
Pronghorn (Antilocapra americana) is a species of artiodactyl (even-toed, hoofed) mammal indigenous to interior western and central North America.
Bitter-tasting and rich in vitamin K, this Mediterranean vegetable with edible buds resembling broccoli is also known as broccoli rabe — what is it?
Rapini (broccoli rabe or raab; RAHB) is a green cruciferous vegetable, with the leaves, buds, and stems all being edible; the buds somewhat resemble broccoli.
Operating under a pseudonym borrowed from The Princess Bride, this American created the first modern darknet marketplace before his 2013 FBI arrest — who is he?
Ross Ulbricht (born March 27, 1984) is an American cybercriminal who created and operated Silk Road, the first modern darknet market, from 2011 until his arrest in 2013.
This American entrepreneur co-founded a pioneering file-sharing service and later became the first president of a social network that would grow into Facebook — who is he?

Sean Parker (born December 3, 1979) is an American entrepreneur and philanthropist, most notable for co-founding the file-sharing computer service Napster, and was the first president of the social networking website Facebook.
Pythons and boas of this limbless reptile group still carry a tiny pelvic girdle and vestigial leg-stubs near the cloaca, hinting at long-lost legs. What animal is this?
Snake are elongated legless reptiles of the suborder Serpentes.
Born in 1955, this former physician left medicine to pursue UFO research, founding an organization dedicated to studying extraterrestrial intelligence — who is he?
Steven M. Greer (born 1955) is an American ufologist and a retired physician.

Known for a leather-like smell when freshly milled and prized for durability and water resistance, this tropical hardwood tree bears small, fragrant white flowers and large, papery, often-hairy leaves — name this tree?
Teak (Tectona grandis) is a tropical hardwood tree species in the family Lamiaceae.

A colorless, sweet-smelling liquid that helps give gasoline and paint fumes their aroma, this benzene relative — a methyl group on a phenyl ring — serves as paint thinner and industrial solvent. What is it?
Toluene is a substituted aromatic hydrocarbon with the chemical formula C6H5CH3, often abbreviated as PhCH3, where Ph stands for the phenyl group.
Native to boreal forests and Arctic tundra across the Northern Hemisphere, this small evergreen heath-family shrub produces edible berries central to Nordic cuisine — what plant is it?
Vaccinium vitis-idaea is a small evergreen shrub in the heath family, Ericaceae. It is known colloquially as the lingonberry, partridgeberry, foxberry, mountain cranberry, or cowberry.
The first person to ever call himself a psychologist, this German founder of modern psychology launched Philosophische Studien, the field's first academic research journal — who is he?
Wilhelm Wundt (16 August 1832 - 31 August 1920) was a German physiologist, philosopher, professor, and one of the fathers of modern psychology.
Also called the belly, this body region sits between the chest and pelvis and is known as the metasoma in arthropods — which body part?
Abdomen: Part of the body between the chest and pelvis. The area occupied by the abdomen is called the abdominal cavity.

Now built by Leonardo but originally developed jointly by an Italian and an American helicopter maker, this 15-seat medium twin-engine helicopter serves VIP transport, firefighting, and search-and-rescue roles — which aircraft?
De Havilland Canada DHC-6 Twin Otter
AgustaWestland AW139: Twin-engined, medium-lift helicopter manufactured by Leonardo.

Believed to be an autoimmune attack on the immune privilege of hair follicles, this condition typically leaves a few coin-sized bald spots — and in rare cases takes every hair on the body. What's it called?
Alopecia areata: Medical condition. Alopecia areata (AA), also known as spot baldness, is a condition in which hair is lost from some or all areas of the body.
Struck off the medical register for 'serious professional misconduct,' this former surgeon authored the fraudulent 1998 Lancet paper falsely tying the MMR vaccine to autism — who is he?
The average adult sheds 50 to 70 billion cells a day through this tidy, programmed cell death — named from a Greek word for 'falling off' — quite unlike messy, traumatic necrosis. What is it?
Apoptosis: Form of programmed cell death. Because apoptosis cannot stop once it has begun, it is a highly regulated process.
One of the oldest of the natural sciences, it leans on math, physics, and chemistry to explain everything from comets to quasars beyond Earth's atmosphere — what field is this?
Astronomy: Scientific study of celestial objects.
The most common type of skin cancer, this slow-growing tumor is sometimes called a 'rodent ulcer' and rarely spreads beyond its original site — what is it?
Basal-cell carcinoma: Most common type of skin cancer. Basal-cell carcinoma (BCC), also known as basal-cell cancer, basalioma, or rodent ulcer, is the most common type of skin cancer.

Having evolved independently at least 94 separate times — first in octocorals some 540 million years ago — this living glow lights up fireflies, deep-sea fish, fungi and dinoflagellates alike; what is it?
Bioluminescence: Emission of light by a living organism.
A synthetic group-7 transition metal made only in particle accelerators, this radioactive element honors a Danish physicist and sits at atomic number 107 — what is it?
Bohrium: Chemical element with atomic number 107 (Bh)

Known also as the Zambezi or Lake Nicaragua species, this aggressive fish can thrive in both salt and fresh water, having been tracked more than 1,100 kilometers up the Mississippi River — what animal is it?
Bull shark: Species of fish. Bull sharks are listed as vulnerable on the IUCN Red List.
Indigenous to the Hindu Kush mountains and grown across Asia and Africa largely for hashish production, this plant species carries far more THC than industrial hemp — which species is it?
Cannabis indica: Species of plant. Cannabis indica is an annual plant species in the family Cannabaceae indigenous to the Hindu Kush mountains of Southern Asia.
Its edible 'curd' is actually a dense head of undeveloped flower buds, and one variety grows its curds in spiral fractal patterns — which vegetable?
Cauliflower: Vegetable in the species Brassica oleracea.
Native to the high Andes and living in colonies called 'herds,' this South American rodent boasts the densest fur of any land mammal — about 20,000 hairs per square centimeter. What is it?
Chinchilla: Rodent genus. The chinchilla is named after the Chincha people of the Andes, who once wore its dense, velvet-like fur and ate its meat.
Sold under the brand name Plavix, this antiplatelet drug taken after a heart attack or coronary stent placement kicks in within two hours and keeps working for five days — what is it?

Clopidogrel: Antiplatelet medication. Clopidogrel, sold under the brand name Plavix among others, is an antiplatelet medication used to reduce the risk of heart disease and stroke in those at high risk.
This towering annual in the daisy family yields the world's fourth most-used vegetable oil, plus snackable seeds and birdseed — and its wild cousins sprout multiple flower heads. What is it?
Common sunflower: Species of flowering plant in the family of Asteraceae.
First identified in Europe and interbreeding with Neanderthals as early as roughly 45,000 years ago, this term describes the earliest known modern humans on the continent — what are they called?
Cro-Magnon: Earliest anatomically modern humans in Europe and West Asia.
Nicknamed the 'Radioactive Boy Scout,' this Michigan teenager built a crude neutron source in a backyard shed while chasing his dream of a homemade nuclear reactor — who is he?
David Hahn: American nuclear radiation enthusiast (1976–2016)

This bacterial infection announces itself with a barking, croup-like cough and a tough grey or white "pseudomembrane" that slowly leathers over the throat and chokes the airway — what is this disease?
Diphtheria: Bacterial disease. Diphtheria is an infection caused by the bacterium Corynebacterium diphtheriae.
Nicknamed the spiny anteater, this quill-covered, egg-laying mammal from Australia and New Guinea has babies called puggles — which creature?

Distinguished by its massive head, huge size, and trademark black facial mask, this gentle British dog breed is now classed as vulnerable in its homeland, with just 104 UK births recorded in 2020 — which breed?
English Mastiff: British breed of dog. The English Mastiff, or simply the Mastiff, is a British breed of very large dog of mastiff type.
This small European finch's male sports a blue-grey cap and rust-red underparts, while both sexes flash white wing bars — what species is it?
Eurasian chaffinch: Species of bird. The Eurasian chaffinch, common chaffinch, or simply the chaffinch (Fringilla coelebs) is a common and widespread small passerine bird – in the finch family.

Marketed under the brand name Captagon, this amphetamine-theophylline combination drug became Syria's largest export under the Assad regime, with tablet stockpiles seized when anti-government forces took Damascus in December 2024. What drug is this?
Fenethylline: Codrug of amphetamine and theophylline. Fenethylline (BAN, USAN) or fenetylline (INN) is a codrug of amphetamine and theophylline and so a mutual prodrug of both.
Named for hindwings that resemble human ears when unfolded, this reddish-brown insect is a common household pest known for the pincers at the tip of its abdomen — which species?
Forficula auricularia: Species of earwig. It is an omnivorous insect belonging to the family Forficulidae.
Often triggered by H. pylori infection or NSAID use, this inflammation of the stomach lining can, in its autoimmune form, lead to pernicious anemia — what condition is it?
Gastritis: Inflammation of the stomach lining. It may occur as a short episode or have a long duration.

Making up about 15% of all brain tumors and thought to arise from cells called astrocytes, this aggressive cancer often announces itself only with vague headaches or sudden personality changes — what is it?
Glioblastoma: Aggressive type of brain cancer. Initial signs and symptoms of glioblastoma are nonspecific.

Native to the Amazon basin, this climbing plant's coffee-bean-sized seeds can be up to 6% caffeine — double a green coffee bean — making it a staple in Brazilian soft drinks and energy drinks — which plant?
Named for the Greek word for the sun, this element makes up about 24% of the universe's elemental mass and has the lowest boiling point of all — which colorless, odorless gas?
Helium: Chemical element with atomic number 2 (He)
Nicknamed 'handy man' for its toolmaking, this archaic human species lived in East and South Africa as far back as 2.4 million years ago — which species?
Homo habilis: Archaic human species from 2.4 to 1.65 mya.

Typically begun with an induction of preliminary instructions, this state of focused attention and heightened suggestibility is debated as either an altered trance or a form of imaginative role-play — what is it?
Hypnosis: State of increased suggestibility. There are competing theories explaining hypnosis and related phenomena.

This analytical framework describes how overlapping identities like race, gender, and class combine to create unique experiences of discrimination or privilege, and emerged partly as a critique of mainstream feminism — which concept?
Intersectionality: Theory of discrimination. The term intersectionality was coined by Kimberlé Crenshaw in 1989.
A French soldier turned naturalist, this early proponent of biological evolution published the three-volume 'Flore françoise' and joined the French Academy of Sciences in 1779 — who is he?
Nicknamed 'Iron Annie,' which corrugated-skin transport plane began life as a 1930 civilian airliner before Nazi Germany converted it for military use?
Nocturnal, owl-faced, and unable to fly, this endangered New Zealand bird holds the title of the world's heaviest parrot. What is it?
Kākāpō: Parrot endemic to New Zealand. It is the only parrot to have a polygynous lek breeding system.
Often beginning in the bone marrow, this group of cancers floods the body with immature 'blast' cells, bringing easy bruising, bone pain, and frequent infections — what is it?
Predominantly black and white with pink and grey highlights, this small Eurasian bird forms social flocks of six to seventeen outside breeding season and often nests in thorny scrub. What is it?
Long-tailed tit: Species of bird in Europe and Asia.

Discovered in 2005 by the same Palomar team whose haul of big, icy Kuiper-belt bodies pushed astronomers to demote Pluto in 2006, this fourth-largest dwarf planet has a methane-frosted, tholin-reddened surface — what is it?
Makemake: Dwarf planet in the Kuiper belt. Makemake (minor-planet number 136472) is a dwarf planet orbiting the Sun in the Kuiper belt, a disc of icy bodies beyond the orbit of Neptune.

First flown in August 1970 and introduced by American Airlines the following year, this trijet wide-body aircraft has two underwing engines and a third mounted at the base of its tail fin — which aircraft?
McDonnell Douglas DC-10: Wide-body three-engine airliner.
Sold under the brand name Medrol, this synthetic steroid can trigger iatrogenic Cushing's syndrome if not carefully tapered after high-dose use for acute flares — name the drug?
Nicknamed 'Viper Zero' and built with a 60/40 Japan-US manufacturing split, this fighter derived from the F-16 was the first combat aircraft to carry an AESA radar — what jet is it?
Mitsubishi F-2: Japanese supersonic jet fighter.

Named for being quieter than its relatives, this large white waterfowl carries an orange beak topped with a black knob that's bigger in males, and is more common in North America than in its native Europe — which bird?
Mute swan: Large species of waterfowl. The mute swan (Cygnus olor) is a species of swan and a member of the family Anatidae within the waterfowl order.
Also known in everyday speech as 'brain surgery,' this medical specialty treats disorders of the brain, spinal cord, and the entire nervous system — what is it called?
Neurosurgery: Medical specialty of disorders which affect any portion of the nervous system.

Producing a distinctive capped nut and supporting more than 950 species of caterpillar, this keystone hardwood genus ranges across the Northern Hemisphere in some 500 species, some evergreen, some deciduous — what tree is it?
Oak: Tree or shrub in the genus Quercus.
A playful, fish-eating cousin of weasels and badgers, this semiaquatic mammal is known for sliding down natural slides and toying with stones — what is it?
A Scottish biologist-turned-town-planner, he coined the word 'conurbation' and gave us one of the earliest versions of 'think globally, act locally' in social science — who was he?
Patrick Geddes: Scottish scientist and town planner (1854–1932)
Usually caused by a virus but sometimes by strep bacteria, this inflammation of the back of the throat brings on a sore throat, fever, and sometimes a hoarse voice — what is it called?
Pharyngitis: Inflammation of the back of the throat. Pharyngitis is a type of upper respiratory tract infection.
Used in randomized clinical trials as a genuine-looking but pharmacologically inert stand-in — like a sugar pill or saline shot — what's this sham treatment called?
Placebo: Substance or treatment of no therapeutic value.
This rare genetic disorder linked to chromosome 15 leaves affected children constantly hungry, often leading to obesity, alongside a narrow forehead and small hands and feet — what is it?
Prader–Willi syndrome: Genetic disorder involving an imprinted genomic region.
This term covers the laws, regulations, and government actions that address issues from education to healthcare to transportation — what is it?
Public policy: Government proposals, principles and actions.
One of the oldest groups of eukaryotic seaweed, this phylum boasts over 7,000 species — mostly marine, though about 5% live in freshwater habitats. What group is it?
Red algae: Division of plant life.

Also called black locust or false acacia, this deciduous legume-family tree is native to just a few small pockets of the United States but has been planted so widely it's now considered invasive elsewhere — which tree?
Robinia pseudoacacia: Species of tree native to North America.
Containing the potent compound salvinorin A, this plant used by Mazatec shamans for spiritual healing sparked a US media panic around 2007 after being shared in online videos — which plant?
Salvia divinorum: Species of plant. The leaves contain the potent compound salvinorin A and can induce a dissociative state and hallucinations.
Ejaculated through the urethra and containing fructose plus enzymes that help sperm survive their journey to fertilize an egg, this bodily fluid is also collected for animal breeding. What is it?
Semen: Reproductive biofluid of male or hermaphroditic animals.
This altered state cycles between REM and non-REM modes, and despite outward stillness it still produces active brain patterns — more reactive than a coma. What is it?
Sleep: Naturally recurring resting state of mind and body.
Lacking any nervous, digestive, or circulatory system, these ancient sea-bound filter feeders pump water through pore-riddled bodies using flagella to survive — what are they?
